thread:
maria_g: Hey team — customer reported structured-output regressions after the model swap last night. Some responses are invalid JSON or have an extra wrapper key (e.g., "result") and the "prediction" field is sometimes null or a different type. Happening intermittently across requests. Repro and raw response below.

alex_h: Thanks. Can you paste a minimal curl and the raw response you got? Also include request id if available.

maria_g: Sure — minimal repro:
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-rlhf-3.1","prompt":"Return JSON with id, prediction, metadata","json_schema":{"type":"object","properties":{"id":{"type":"string"},"prediction":{"type":"string"},"metadata":{"type":"object"}}},"stream":false}'
```
Raw body we received:
```
{"id":"abc-123","result":{"prediction":null},"metadata":{}}
```
This used to come back as `{"id":"abc-123","prediction":"...","metadata":{}}` on 3.0. Request id: r-98765, header x-model: redwood-rlhf-3.1-quant.

alex_h: Ok that shows two problems: a wrapper `result` was added and `prediction` is null (type changed). Did the customer hit any retries or different regions? Any custom routing or model variant rules on the project?

maria_g: They're not using routing rules, single route, region us-west1. No retries. Latency observed higher too (~60ms increase). They say behavior started ~1793449000.

ingram: I can see a canary deploy around 1793444987 by deploy-bot with commit d4f1c2. Deploy note: "enable-wrapper-handling" — tagging @eng_mike since this sounds related to model output normalization.

deploy-bot: canary deploy d4f1c2 -> svc/inference-canvas at 1793444987 (notes: enable-wrapper-handling)

eng_mike: Investigating now. We introduced an "auto-wrap" normalization to handle conversational model outputs that sometimes return pre-wrapped objects. Looks like for some quantized variants the model already returns object under `result` and we double-wrap -> breaks strict JSON schema consumers. Also saw a branch where empty generation ends up as `null` instead of empty string.

alex_h: Short-term mitigation: ask the customer to pin to redwood-rlhf-3.0 or add a request header to avoid normalization. You can set `model: "redwood-rlhf-3.0"` in the call or add header `X-Output-Normalization: off` (internal temporary flag). I'll escalate.

maria_g: Customer wants rollback if that's safest. How do we pin on their side quickly?

alex_h: They can change the model field in the payload to `redwood-rlhf-3.0` — that's fastest. From Console: Project -> Routes -> Edit route -> Model override = redwood-rlhf-3.0. I'll create an internal incident INF-2026 and link here.

sre-ops: Note: if some backends are still on 3.1 and others on 3.0, we could see schema drift at the edge due to sticky connections. We're scheduling a rolling restart of the inference pool for the service to remove mixed-version backends.

eng_mike: Patch prepared to avoid double-wrap for structured-output endpoints; adding tests for pre-wrapped responses and null->empty-string normalization. Will push hotfix to canary and confirm.

maria_g: Thanks — I'll relay the pin instructions and the temporary header to the customer. Please post when fix is in canary so I can update them. :thumbsup:

alex_h: Filed INF-2026 for tracking. Assigning to eng_mike and sre-ops. Will update when canary shows green.

eng_mike: Can confirm hotfix pushed to canary at 1793456800 — disabling auto-wrap for endpoints using `json_schema`. Running regression tests now.

maria_g: Got it. I will retest with their payload after canary green. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

sre-ops: Rolling restart started at 1793456815. Should converge within ~10m.

maria_g: Closing loop with customer, sending repro and ticket INF-2026.
